turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, do not test my patience any further. Your actions have consequences, and I will not hesitate to take action to protect my people and my land.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I couldn't help but notice the tension between you both. Perhaps it would be wiser to focus on finding a resolution rather than escalating the situation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You, Nikhil, are always so eager to prove your bravery. But, I must ask, have you seen the latest crop yields? I think your people would be more concerned about the withering fields than about my presence.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have seen the crop yields, Sandip, and I know what they mean. It is a sign of the larger problems facing our region, and I will not let petty squabbles distract me from addressing them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, I think we should also consider the impact of our rivalry on the local economy and the people who depend on us for livelihood.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, always the voice of reason, but I'm afraid Nikhil here is too busy with his war drums to listen.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, do not underestimate the threat of the Mussulmans. Their discontent will not be silenced by your scorn or dismissal.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, what do you think is the root cause of the Mussulmans' discontent? Is it truly just a matter of our rivalry, or are there deeper issues at play?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, you're not still convinced that the entire region is about to erupt into chaos, are you? I'm the one they fear, not you, with your musty old records and dusty predictions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your flippant remarks, Sandip. The records I keep are not dusty, but rather a testament to the meticulous care I take in managing my estate.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, have you considered the possibility that Nikhil's concerns are not entirely unfounded? Perhaps it's time for us to engage in a more nuanced discussion about the issues facing our region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You're starting to sound like a village elder, Nikhil, warning of impending doom. I'm a poet, not a prophet, so spare me the dire predictions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not indulge in petty banter with you, Sandip. The threat is real, and I will not stand idly by while our people are put in harm's way.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, how do you think we can mitigate the risks you've mentioned? What steps can we take to protect our people and our lands?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, always the voice of reason, aren't you? I suppose it's too much to hope that Nikhil's doomsday prophecies will come to naught, but I'll play along – what's the worst that could happen, hmm?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not making idle threats, Sandip. The Mussulmans have been restless, and I've received credible information about their plans to attack our villages. I demand that you take this seriously and take steps to protect our people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I'd like to know more about the information you've received. Can you tell me more about the specific threats you've heard?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always the self-appointed guardian of our village's safety, while I'm just a carefree zamindar, lounging in my palace, waiting for your latest catastrophe to unfold. What's the betting, I'll be the one who saves the day, as always?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I warn you, do not underestimate the threat. We cannot afford to be complacent in the face of danger.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I understand your concern, and I'd like to know more about the information you've received. What specific actions do you propose we take to protect our people?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
